MAJOR: Merge-gate enforcement is claimed in AC but no merge-gate file/owner appears in affected_files/components (only gate1_check/gate_decisions); CL-001 route-by-kind not answered — who single-writes merge enforcement?
DEFERRED requires "an existing backlog id": design never states where/ how existence is validated (cross-store lookup, offline cache), so a stale/foreign id passes the policy check.
HIL DISPOSITION_APPROVAL binds "finding sigs" but findings are reviewer-owned (CL-002); design does not state where sigs come from or how reviewer-owned findings are read-only for the main thread.

Backfill/grandfathering for existing completed items without ac_verification/final_report is only listed as a risk, not a decided invariant; forward-looking guard can silently split behavior across the same store schema.
No single canonical writer specified for disposition state: policy code, gate checks, and finalize_item.py all touch it — duplicate logic/owner risk (CL-001, reuse).
MINOR: Guardrail 10 not addressed: no stated metrics/log lines on gate refusals (missing AC, disallowed disposition, absent final_report), making production failures hard to diagnose.

Guardrail 4/6 partial: rollback is "revert commit" but no statement that in-flight items mid-completion recover cleanly if the diff is interrupted (migration-interrupted recovery checklist item unanswered).
cost_source is persisted but its trust level/provenance is undefined; unattributed cost undermines long-term auditability.
"accepted/deferred with ids" in final_report conflicts with ACCEPTED being prohibited — accepted is permanently empty; schema should state that invariant explicitly.
Language rule (checklist 7) not explicitly asserted: confirm any new shipped logic lands in Go and core/execution_trail.py changes are edits only, not new shipped Python logic.
Test taxonomy mapping (unit/api/db/logic/go/other) needs a stated, tested precedence rule (e.g., go vs unit) to avoid unstable classification across runners.
NIT: No coverage named for the show-render paths of AC verification and test-by-kind tables (recurring MINOR class: render helpers untested).
Guardrail 9 (tenant/RLS) is not addressed in the design text; state explicitly as not-applicable rather than leaving it silent.
docs/REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE.md update is bundled in the same diff as enforcement — consider ordering so docs land with the contract, not after.
SUMMARY: Verdict: directionally sound and reversible, but the enforcement ownership map is incomplete (merge gate, single writer for disposition state) and validation of DEFERRED backlog ids/HIL finding-sig provenance is unspecified — those are the top risks to close before Gate 1.5.
Secondary risks: grandfathering of legacy items, undefined refusal observability, and test-classification precedence.
